The before/after preview is refreshed with it (skill before-after-preview). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_ReviseEdit . Those are server processes in smart-trust; this step records that the parties started them. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/dsa-document-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_EndDuties . Root-cause the failure candidate, extracted "Flake" is not a root cause. A red PR is work now, whatever its review state — only a green, mergeable head waits on reviewers. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_Diagnose . Round-trip translation QA candidate, extracted Bean: folio-assistant-ktt2 Back-translates target-language .md to source language and compares meaning. Distinguishes semantic drift from terminology misses. Tool: translation_validate MCP tool No gateway follows: drift or clean, the translation goes to Task_SMEReview with the findings attached. Which of two readings is right is a human call (translation-manager, "route drift to a human reviewer"), and every translation in this workflow is reviewed and signed off anyway, so a clean result is evidence for the reviewer and never a way around them. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/human-translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_RoundTripQA . Round-trip translation QA candidate, extracted Back-translate each localized narrative into its source language and compare the meaning, to catch semantic drift and bad terminology that a forward-only check cannot see. Agentic, by the owner's ruling of 2026-10-06 (bean ktt2). Two parties are kept apart under untainted-verification: a back-translator that sees ONLY the target-language text, and an adjudicator that sees the original and the back-translation and rules. The verdict is recorded per block, under criterion translation-semantic-roundtrip in the block's <block>.<locale>.translation-qa.json sidecar, by the translation-roundtrip-record Tool (translation-manager §5). A terminology miss is a different criterion, translation-terms-preserved (acronyms, numbers, URLs that must survive), so Gateway_Drift can tell the two apart. Never close this step by reversing the PO's msgid→msgstr map: that returns the source exactly and scores 1.0 always. An empty translation-semantic-roundtrip entry list means "not yet run", which is never a pass. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-l1-completeness-gate.bpmn#Task_RoundTrip . Round-trip translation QA (back-translate) candidate, extracted Bean: folio-assistant-ktt2 Back-translates the target-language .md into the source language and compares meaning with the original. Detects semantic drift and terminology misses that a forward-only fluency check cannot see. Tool: translation_validate MCP tool . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_RoundTripQA . Route it, and watch the queue candidate, extracted A file goes to ingestion; a link or a description goes to whatever will resolve it. Acquisition stops here — the moment a file is in the queue, library-ingestion owns it, and keeping that seam sharp is what lets a resource acquired through a channel that does not exist yet reach ingestion unchanged. An arrival may be minutes or days away, so it is watched rather than chased. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/content-acquisition.bpmn#A_Route . Run check:ci-health, WRITING the report file candidate, extracted Run check:ci-health --out, writing the report file before any exit path. Exit 0 clean, 1 live failures, 2 could not check. bun also exits 1 on an uncaught exception, so an exit 1 with no report file is a crash and is treated as could-not-check. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/ci-health-watch.bpmn#Task_Check . Run check:requirements schema, collision, and lineage gate candidate, extracted Run bun run cat check:requirements to verify schema conformance (bootstrap/schemas/requirement.schema.json), slug uniqueness across docs/proposals/ and docs/requirements/, acyclicity of derivedFrom, existence of all referenced derivedFrom / dependsOn / supersededBy / skills / processes targets, and RequirementSet sign-off invariants. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/requirements-filing.bpmn#A_RunCheck . Run every verifier over the export candidate, extracted Run the verifier set (scripts/publish-verify.ts, bun run cat publish:verify -- --dir <site>) over the built tree. A SET: each verifier is one entry, and adding one changes nothing else. The first is JSON-LD expansion under a real processor, network refused — a property the context does not declare, a relative IRI or a context that will not load is a finding. Only documents of OURS are verified; third-party data in the tree is counted and cannot block. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/publish-verification.bpmn#A_Verify . Run final IG Publisher build and verify candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/SGAuthoring.DAKLifecycle.bpmn#Task_FinalBuild . Run IG Publisher build candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/SGAuthoring.DAKLifecycle.bpmn#Task_RunBuild . Run placement, and raise a bean for the authoring candidate, extracted The offer produces a DECISION, not a node. placement then decides instance, graph and node kind — it is the step that catches a hardcoded path or a literal naming one folio — and the authoring itself becomes a bean, because work here is a bean before it is a file. op="note" and not create, for the reason A_CreateBeans above states: the engine has no create op — it claims, notes and resolves the instance's OWN bean. The agent mints the authoring bean itself with beans create, running the exact-title existence check first, and what this step records is a note that the decision was taken. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-signoff.bpmn#A_RecordKg . Run publication QA gates [content-test] candidate, extracted Publication-readiness QA across layers — QC reports, IG Publisher QA, proof status, broken links, build warnings. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/draft-to-publication.bpmn#Task_PublicationQa . Run reuse-first lookup and record candidates [classify-and-code-content · recommendation-scenarios · glossary-terms] candidate, extracted Run the terminology-lookup Tool across the four reuse-first rungs of the terminology-coding methodology: (1) target guide vocabulary, (2) smart-base generic personas, GRADE code lists and guideline-domain glossary, (3) external WHO-FIC/ILO standards (ICD-11, ICHI/CDHIv2, ISCO-08, ATC), and (4) local glossary candidate (status: candidate, source: extracted) or could-not-determine for business-process with its WARNING line. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/classify-and-code-content.bpmn#Task_LookupAndCode . Run the component's checker [content-validate · content-test] candidate, extracted The mechanical checks for this component, before anyone is asked (skill l2-component-edit-review, column "checker"): BPMN imports in bpmn-js with no warnings and its lanes map to personas (dak-swimlanes.ts); DMN loads, its decisions are reachable (artefact-reachability, audit:reachability) and its test cases run (content-test); the data dictionary web annex's ids are unique and its references and terminology bindings resolve (check-web-annexes.ts); personas, scenarios and requirements each trace to an L1 recommendation (recommendation-extraction's implementedBy edges). Findings travel with the review request; a failing check does not stop the hand-on, it is a finding the reviewer sees. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/l2-component-edit-review.bpmn#Task_Check . Run the gate set on the train [code-quality-gates] candidate, extracted Every gate CI runs, on the combination (R2): a member that passes alone can still break main with another. The merge-gate epic (nok9, #1887) adds its gates here when they land. The release security gate (bun run cat security:gate, bean ieum) is one of them: it runs inside the gate set, so no train merges past a blocking security finding or a security check that could not run. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-train.bpmn#Call_Gates . Run the gates against the merge of head into base candidate, extracted CI tests the MERGE, not the branch. That is why a locally green tree can go red here: the agent's tree and the merge result are different trees, and the difference is invisible from a checkout. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_RunCI . Run the health checks, keeping the report either way candidate, extracted Run bun run cat health --out and upload the JSON report whatever the verdict — on unknown it is the only evidence of why the sweep went blind. Exit 0 clean, 1 gating findings, 2 could not check; exit 1 with no report is a crash. The checks report and never act: every finding names something a person does. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/repository-health-watch.bpmn#Task_Check . Run the node audits candidate, extracted check:tools, kg:audit and typecheck. Read the kg-qa sidecar rather than the summary: it is written per node so an inherited defect and a new one are distinguishable. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/review-code.bpmn#Task_RunNodeAudits . Run the platform's own gates candidate, extracted Before pushing, not after CI says so. bun test passing is NOT the gates passing: measured 2026-09-19, a green unit suite sat beside a tsc failure and a missing @graphNode tag, and the second broke a QA sidecar comparison as well — one cause, two symptoms, and an agent running only the tests would have pushed all three. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/code-change-review.bpmn#Task_RunGates . Run the release security gate [security:gate] candidate, extracted bun run cat security:gate, before anything is built (bean ieum, owner 2026-10-07: "security check before release"). It runs every security check this repository has by name: workflow injection, secret leaks, lockfile and toolchain pins, QA reviewer permission, materialised fixity, and third-party action SHA pinning outside staging-only workflows. Each is reported as pass, fail or unknown. A blocking fail OR unknown refuses the publish, because could-not-check is never clean. Until this step existed, no publish or merge process named any security check; they ran only inside the CI gate set. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/docs-site-publish.bpmn#Task_SecurityGate . Run the row's gates tests · e2e · site-links candidate, extracted The mvp commands declared for this tenant. For the theme: bun test, CI=1 bunx playwright test (a11y, action tiles, sidebar panels, QA panel) and scripts/site-links.ts --site ./_site, which checks the navbar tiles against the BUILT site rather than against the attribute — the distinction that let a 404 ship unnoticed once already. A red gate is EVIDENCE, not an exit. It does not end the process and it does not loop by itself: "this version breaks us" is a finding the decider needs, not a reason to stop before they see it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#Task_Gates . Run the rule's mechanical half candidate, extracted Whatever patterns and terminology the rule carries. A judgementOnly rule has no mechanical half by declaration, which is different from nobody having written one yet. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/voice-review.bpmn#Task_MechanicalHalf .

6474.title: S
6474.content: Say it could not be confirmed candidate, extracted No URL, no probe, or a failed request. Reported as "could not check", never as "not yet" and never as "live". BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_ReportUnknown . Say what is being decided, and why it matters now candidate, extracted First, and in the message itself: where you are (the Process and task, as which Role, asking whom — from the three determinations), what the decision is, what depends on it, and what is already known — each fact with where it came from. A link is where somebody goes for more; it is never where the terms are defined. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_GiveContext . Say what is needed, and ask for a link OR a description candidate, extracted Both forms, named together. A person who cannot find the file often knows exactly what it is, and a description in their own words is an acquired resource rather than a consolation prize. Asking for the upload first demands the one thing they may not have, before the cheaper answers have been offered. Say what happens if they do nothing. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/content-acquisition.bpmn#A_Ask . Say what moved and where it went candidate, extracted Tell the reader what moved and where it went, so the content can be found in the trashcan rather than inferred missing from a card that disappeared. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-relocate.bpmn#A_ReportMove . Say where it will be candidate, extracted A measured 404. The author is told the address and that the first build has not landed there yet — which is useful, and is not the same as being told it is live. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_ReportPending . Scaffold the folio (folio_init) candidate, extracted content/, uploads/, library/, the first manifests, <slug>.json and index.config.json (the instance's config inline in its entry; no <slug>.config.json, bean ymvt), the builder shim, AGENTS.md with its stubs, .mcp.json, the session-start hook and the beans store. On the overlay path it declares in index.config.json exactly the markers picked at Task_ChooseHarnessed, and none it was not given. Refuses rather than overwrites when a folio is already present. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_Scaffold . Scan open issues for match candidate, extracted Search open issues, then recently closed ones, by title and body keywords for one this request belongs to. Requirements may span several issues; note every relevant one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-issue-linking.bpmn#A_ScanIssues . Scan the environment opportunities and threats candidate, extracted The external axis, first, per Weihrich. Work the source's categories of environmental change rather than free-associating: societal, governmental, economic, competitive, supplier and market changes, each item recorded with what it impacts. An opportunity is an external element that gives benefit; a threat is one that could cause trouble. Both are outside the subject and largely beyond its control — that is what puts them on this axis, not whether they feel good or bad. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_ScanExternal . Scan the repo for content worth importing candidate, extracted Read-only. Classifies candidates into library/ (external source) and content/ (authored here), and reports what it could not classify as its own bucket rather than forcing every file into one of the two. Its fourth section, markers, lists the content markers it found — sushi-config.yaml, a legacy dak.json, .bpmn processes, a beans store, library/, Lean, folio manifests — each with its paths, whether index.config.json already declares it (declared, not-declared, or unknown), and the snippet that would. bun run cat-harness-tools/scripts/scan-repo-content.ts --json, a plain command any agent host can run. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/conduct/getting-started.bpmn#Task_ScanRepo . Scan the subject strengths and weaknesses candidate, extracted The internal axis. Work the source's functional checklist rather than a blank page: marketing, research and development, management information systems, management team, operations, finance, human resources. A strength gives advantage over others in the field; a weakness places the subject at a disadvantage relative to others. Both are attributes OF the subject. The source's warning belongs to this step specifically: listing strengths on paper "is very different from testing the organization and experiencing the strengths at work", so a strength recorded here is a claim, and where evidence for it exists it is cited. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_ScanInternal . Schema and constraint checks [content-validate] candidate, extracted Block schema, label prefixes, required fields, constraint rules. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/editing-hci-validation.bpmn#Task_SchemaValidate . Scope the criterion so it stops applying here candidate, extracted One edit to the criterion rather than ten overrules on the blocks it should never have covered. This branch is the one an adjudicator under time pressure converts into a dispensation, and the conversion is a defect: a dispensation lapses when the source moves, so a mis-scoped criterion granted its way past comes back every time anybody touches the block. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/criterion-adjudication.bpmn#A_ScopeCriterion . Scope the DAK [content-plan] candidate, extracted Enumerate the processes, decisions and data elements the guideline implies; identify the actors. BPMN activities of smart-base · source smart-base/processes/content/l2-dak-authoring.bpmn#Task_ScopeDak . Scope the delta pinned → candidate candidate, extracted Restricted to the directories that reach our output — for a Jekyll theme _sass, _includes, _layouts, assets. Upstream's own docs, CI and tests cannot reach us, and counting them makes a harmless release look alarming. The changelog is the claim; git diff --stat pinned..candidate over those paths is the evidence. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn#A_Scope . Scope the sample: which items, which store, and is it PERMANENT? candidate, extracted Three answers, recorded before anything is fetched. WHICH ITEMS: named by the source's identifiers, or by a subset strategy its descriptor supports. WHICH STORE: the knowledge graph or other structured store the import is tested against. PERMANENT OR TRIAL: a permanent sample lands in library/ and is refreshed; a trial lands in fsh-guts/ and is not. The purpose materialize-remote asks for (working or archival) is asked there, not here. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/library/sample-import.bpmn#Task_Scope . Scrap the bean, with the reason candidate, extracted The agent's own beans update --status scrapped; never deleted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/sdlc/merge-refusal.bpmn#Task_Scrap . Scrap with reasons NEVER delete candidate, extracted status: scrapped, plus a "Reasons for Scrapping" section. This is what "disable" means here — the CLI has no disabled state; its vocabulary is draft, todo, in-progress, completed, scrapped. The agent's own beans update; the engine has no scrap op. DELETION IS NEVER THE ANSWER, even though beans delete exists. A scrapped bean records that the work was considered and rejected, and why; a deleted one leaves a sibling session unable to tell abandonment from accident, and leaves the next agent free to re-open the same dead end. READ OFF THAT IG rather than from general knowledge: a GDHCN trustlist distributes KEY MATERIAL as W3C DID documents, and says nothing about what you wrap your bytes in — the health-certificate envelope is a separate specification in the same IG, and a document package is not a health certificate. So what is settled is where a verifier GETS THE KEY, not what it verifies. A portal that can fetch the bytes but not reach the trustlist cannot verify, which is unknown and not a failure — air-gapped is a declared deployment value, so that case is answered rather than assumed away. Still OPEN and unread: the rotation and revocation model, and whether a document-package signature can be expressed for a GDHCN-aware verifier at all. Two schemes with different properties remain to choose between, and the trustlist does not choose between them. A PACKAGE signature over the manifest verifies the SET — nothing added, removed or altered — and must be reissued whenever any file changes. A PER-ASSET signature verifies one file independently, which is what an edge cache serving one asset can actually check, and it cannot detect a removal because there is nothing left to verify. (NOT A GATE) candidate, extracted Bean qbco, issue #2456 (owner, 2026-10-07: "1y, 2y, 3y, 4y"). On a PUSH to main only; on any other event it is skipped and nothing waits for it. A merge-button merge of an up-to-date PR carries a tree CI has already tested. verdict-reuse.sh looks up the runs of this workflow on the merged head (the merge commit's second parent) and answers reuse=true only when one concluded success, ran every job a reuse would skip, and tested exactly this tree: for a pull_request run, the tested-tree: its Task_QaWorkingCopy job wrote into its check run's summary; for a dispatch, the head's own tree. Then the four bun test shards (part of Task_TypeScript), the three e2e shards (Task_E2E) and the standalone ratchet (part of Task_RepositoryGates) are skipped on this push, and the summary names the run whose verdict stands. Everything that judges the tree against main or reads qa-reports still runs. A squash, an API error, a missing record or a mismatch is reuse=false and every job runs: could-not-determine is never green. Drawn before the fork because the jobs it can skip wait for it; the others do not. Since the same ruling, a newer push to main also cancels an older main run still in progress (the workflow's concurrency), so main's verdict history is thinned by decision. WHO's own trust network is therefore the same shape as this diagram one layer down, which is the strongest argument the design has. The stage that gets dropped, because every other stage produces something visible and this one produces nothing when it passes. 6480.title: Glossary: Tools
6480.content: Candidate terms extracted from every Tool node: title as the label, description as the definition, the Tool id as the code. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: cat-harness-tools 1 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 33 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 16 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-sci 25 (SKOS) · smart-base 14 (SKOS) · who-iris 1 (SKOS). 6508.content: handover-report candidate, extracted Write a handover report: a templated snapshot of an agent's current state, committed as a bean note, so that a session or subagent that stalls, runs out of context, or loses its container can be picked up by another agent without re-deriving anything. Use it when you are told a stall is likely, at the end of every long arc, before a risky or long-running step, and whenever a steward asks for one. Its reader is stalled-agent-triage. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/sdlc/sdlc-core/handover-report.md . harness-projections candidate, extracted Who may write under .claude/, and when. The generated projections of the knowledge graph (.claude/commands/*.md from skill:commands, the assembled agent memory under .claude/agents/ and .claude/agent-memory/) are written by CI, which commits them to the PR branch, and never by an agent. A hand-edited .claude/ file (settings.json, its hooks, a hand-written command or agent definition) changes only with the owner's explicit consent to that change: the agent shows the exact diff and the reason, asks first, and records the consent. Read before staging any path under .claude/. Read before declaring a directory, before adding a graph typology, and when reading check:subgraph-coverage. Carries which obligations are ranked as unmet promises rather than unanswered questions, why the discriminator is "is this the static knowledge graph", and which single obligation a harness may never waive. Skills of cat-harness · source cat-harness/skills/kg/kg-core/harness-requirements.md . harness-tiles candidate, extracted A tile is a function of the harness watching a directory, not of nodes. Where the tile set comes from, what a tile opens, and the two gaps it reports rather than hides. Then context, the options, a recommendation and what happens with no answer, then ONE question. The reusable discussion every bootstrap diagram calls when it needs a person; it records the answer, an applied default, or what is still open, and never a guess. 6525.title: Glossary: DMN decisions
6525.content: Candidate terms extracted from every DMN decision: name as the label, its own <description> as the definition, the element id as the code. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: cat-harness 10 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 4 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-sci 1 (SKOS). Size: this page holds 15 terms and is 12 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 15 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 15 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 15 shown . A B D E I R S W

6540.content: health system strengthening A guideline whose recommendations address how the health system itself is organised and resourced — service delivery, health workforce, health information systems, access to medical products, financing, and leadership and governance — rather than a particular condition or population intervention. Educational institutions may also be operated by private organizations, such as religious bodies, special interest groups or private educational and training enterprises, both for-profit and not-for-profit. (108) Types of health workforce education and training institutions are: • Public: Public educational institutions provide core educational services such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres. They are controlled and managed directly by a public education authority or governing body (council, committee, etc.), the majority of whose members are appointed by a public authority. • Private: Private educational institutions provide core educational products such as teaching activities and ancillary services. 6548.title: F
6548.content: Facility Type candidate Facility types are categorized following the system of health accounts through the classification of health care industries. These enable arrangement of country-specific institutions in common, internationally applicable categories. The categories are as follows: Hospitals (HP.1) Hospitals comprise licensed establishments that are primarily engaged in providing medical, diagnostic and treatment services that include physician, nursing and other health services to inpatients and the specialised accommodation services required by inpatients. Hospitals provide inpatient health services, many of which can be delivered only by using specialised facilities and professional knowledge as well as advanced medical technology and equipment, which form a significant and integral part of the provision process. Although the principal activity is the provision of inpatient medical care they may also provide day care, outpatient and home health care services. The tasks of hospitals may vary by country and are usually defined by legal requirements. In some countries, health care facilities need in addition a minimum size (such as a number of beds and medical staff to guarantee 24-hour access) in order to be registered as a hospital. Residential long-term care facilities (HP.2) The category of Residential long-term care facilities comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing residential long-term care that combines nursing, supervisory or other types of care as required by the residents. In these establishments, a significant part of the production process and the care provided is a mix of health and social services, with the health services being largely at the level of nursing care, in combination with personal care services. The medical components of care are, however, much less intensive than those provided in hospitals. Providers of ambulatory health care (HP.3) This item comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing health care services directly to outpatients who do not require inpatient services. This includes both offices of general medical practitioners and medical specialists and establishments specialising in the treatment of day-cases and in the delivery of home care services. Health practitioners in ambulatory health care primarily provide services to patients who visit the health professional’s office, or the practitioners visit the patients at home. Consequently, these establishments do not usually provide inpatient services. Ancillary services (HP.4, including transportation, emergency rescue, laboratories and others) This category comprises establishments that provide specific ancillary type of services directly to outpatients under the supervision of health professionals and not covered within the episode of treatment by hospitals, nursing care facilities, ambulatory care providers or other providers. Included are providers of patient transportation and emergency rescue, medical and diagnostic laboratories, dental laboratories and other providers of ancillary services. These specialised providers may charge patients directly for their services rendered or may provide these ancillary services as benefits-in-kind under special service contracts. Retailers (HP.5, including pharmacies) This item comprises specialised establishments whose primary activity is the retail sale of medical goods to the general public for individual or household consumption or utilisation. Establishments whose primary activity is the manufacture of medical goods, such as making lenses, orthopaedic or prosthetic appliances for direct sale to the general public for individual or household use, are also included, as is fitting and repair done in combination with sale. Note: Due to special medical safety and quality regulations, retailers of over-the-counter medical products and other providers of medical goods are subject to licensing and/or pharmaceutical authorisation in order to be eligible to provide their activities. Non-health care products such as cosmetics, dietetic products and natural products are excluded from health expenditures. Providers of preventive care (HP.6) This category comprises organisations that primarily provide collective preventive programmes and campaigns/public health programmes for specific groups of individuals or the population-at-large, such as health promotion and protection agencies or public health institutes as well as specialised establishments providing primary preventive care as their principal activity. This includes the promotion of healthy living conditions and lifestyles in schools by special outside health care professionals, agencies or organisations. This includes norms, behaviours and roles associated with being a woman, man, girl or boy, as well as relationships with each other. The handbook cites its reference 48 for this entry. | Facility Type (National health workforce accounts: a handbook, second edition (2023))Facility types are categorized following the system of health accounts through the classification of health care industries. These enable arrangement of country-specific institutions in common, internationally applicable categories. The categories are as follows: Hospitals (HP.1) Hospitals comprise licensed establishments that are primarily engaged in providing medical, diagnostic and treatment services that include physician, nursing and other health services to inpatients and the specialised accommodation services required by inpatients. Hospitals provide inpatient health services, many of which can be delivered only by using specialised facilities and professional knowledge as well as advanced medical technology and equipment, which form a significant and integral part of the provision process. Although the principal activity is the provision of inpatient medical care they may also provide day care, outpatient and home health care services. The tasks of hospitals may vary by country and are usually defined by legal requirements. In some countries, health care facilities need in addition a minimum size (such as a number of beds and medical staff to guarantee 24-hour access) in order to be registered as a hospital. Residential long-term care facilities (HP.2) The category of Residential long-term care facilities comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing residential long-term care that combines nursing, supervisory or other types of care as required by the residents. In these establishments, a significant part of the production process and the care provided is a mix of health and social services, with the health services being largely at the level of nursing care, in combination with personal care services. The medical components of care are, however, much less intensive than those provided in hospitals. Providers of ambulatory health care (HP.3) This item comprises establishments that are primarily engaged in providing health care services directly to outpatients who do not require inpatient services. This includes both offices of general medical practitioners and medical specialists and establishments specialising in the treatment of day-cases and in the delivery of home care services. Health practitioners in ambulatory health care primarily provide services to patients who visit the health professional’s office, or the practitioners visit the patients at home. Consequently, these establishments do not usually provide inpatient services. Ancillary services (HP.4, including transportation, emergency rescue, laboratories and others) This category comprises establishments that provide specific ancillary type of services directly to outpatients under the supervision of health professionals and not covered within the episode of treatment by hospitals, nursing care facilities, ambulatory care providers or other providers. Included are providers of patient transportation and emergency rescue, medical and diagnostic laboratories, dental laboratories and other providers of ancillary services. These specialised providers may charge patients directly for their services rendered or may provide these ancillary services as benefits-in-kind under special service contracts. Retailers (HP.5, including pharmacies) This item comprises specialised establishments whose primary activity is the retail sale of medical goods to the general public for individual or household consumption or utilisation. Establishments whose primary activity is the manufacture of medical goods, such as making lenses, orthopaedic or prosthetic appliances for direct sale to the general public for individual or household use, are also included, as is fitting and repair done in combination with sale. Note: Due to special medical safety and quality regulations, retailers of over-the-counter medical products and other providers of medical goods are subject to licensing and/or pharmaceutical authorisation in order to be eligible to provide their activities. Non-health care products such as cosmetics, dietetic products and natural products are excluded from health expenditures. Providers of preventive care (HP.6) This category comprises organisations that primarily provide collective preventive programmes and campaigns/public health programmes for specific groups of individuals or the population-at-large, such as health promotion and protection agencies or public health institutes as well as specialised establishments providing primary preventive care as their principal activity. This includes the promotion of healthy living conditions and lifestyles in schools by special outside health care professionals, agencies or organisations. Educational institutions may also be operated by private organizations, such as religious bodies, special interest groups or private educational and training enterprises, both for-profit and not-for-profit. (108) Types of health workforce education and training institutions are: • Public: Public educational institutions provide core educational services such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres. They are controlled and managed directly by a public education authority or governing body (council, committee, etc.), the majority of whose members are appointed by a public authority. • Private: Private educational institutions provide core educational products such as teaching activities and ancillary services. They include schools, colleges, universities, and training centres, that are controlled and directly managed either by a private organization such as a church, trade union, or business enterprise, or by a governing board whose members have mostly not been selected by a public authority. A school, for example, could in theory be entirely publicly funded but still be considered private because it is not managed by the government. Public Health Workforce candidate The public health workforce comprises all individuals who contribute to the delivery of at least one of the essential public health functions as part of integrated services and systems. 6557.title: Q
6557.content: quality of the evidence In the context of guideline development, the confidence that the estimates of an effect are adequate to support a particular decision or recommendation. Rated high, moderate, low or very low. The WHO handbook for guideline development (2nd edition, §9.1, p. 122) names both alternatives: "Alternative terms to describe the quality of the evidence are 'certainty of the evidence' or 'confidence in the estimates of effect'." The handbook uses 'quality of the evidence' 77 times and 'certainty of the evidence' once; the who-guideline-development voice and the platform's `grade-certainty` code list use 'certainty', GRADE's later name. Rated for a body of evidence per outcome, never for a single study. Not the strength of a recommendation, which the handbook keeps apart throughout. Remuneration candidate Average gross annual income earned by employees or those self-employed, i.e. income per year and per person, before any deductions are made for social security contributions or income tax. A person may have more than one qualifying job in any given reference period. • Income earned by employees (earnings) refers to all payments – in cash or in kind, for work done or time worked – made by their employers, and includes basic wages, overtime and other bonuses (such as for night work, work on weekends), all allowances paid by the employer (such as for working away from home or for housing) and all commissions and gratuities paid by the employer. Employers may be the government, corporations, non-profit institutions or households. • Income earned by self-employed workers refers to all payments, in cash or in kind, made by customers for goods or services, and includes capitation or fee-for-service reimbursement, bonuses, commissions, and gratuities. It should be net of operation costs/practice expenses. From the Glossary of the handbook (p. 92; PDF page 106). 6591.title: Glossary: Schema fields, T–Z
6591.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 44 (SKOS) · cat-harness-tools 2233 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 141 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 181 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-sci 49 (SKOS) · smart-base 13 (SKOS). One of 7 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 455 terms and is 264 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2661 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2661 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 455 shown . T U V W

6597.title: Glossary: Schema fields, S
6597.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 44 (SKOS) · cat-harness-tools 2233 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 141 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 181 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-sci 49 (SKOS) · smart-base 13 (SKOS). One of 7 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 248 terms and is 144 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2661 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2661 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 248 shown . S

6600.title: Glossary: Schema fields, A–C
6600.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 44 (SKOS) · cat-harness-tools 2233 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 141 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 181 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-sci 49 (SKOS) · smart-base 13 (SKOS). One of 7 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 492 terms and is 293 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2661 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2661 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 492 shown . A B C

6605.title: Glossary: Schema fields, D–E
6605.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 44 (SKOS) · cat-harness-tools 2233 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 141 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 181 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-sci 49 (SKOS) · smart-base 13 (SKOS). One of 7 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 211 terms and is 125 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2661 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2661 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 211 shown . D E

6609.title: Glossary: Schema fields, P–R
6609.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 44 (SKOS) · cat-harness-tools 2233 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 141 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 181 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-sci 49 (SKOS) · smart-base 13 (SKOS). One of 7 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 517 terms and is 302 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2661 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2661 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 517 shown . P Q R

6614.title: Glossary: Schema fields, M–O
6614.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 44 (SKOS) · cat-harness-tools 2233 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 141 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 181 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-sci 49 (SKOS) · smart-base 13 (SKOS). One of 7 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 213 terms and is 129 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 2661 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 2661 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 213 shown . M N O

6619.title: Glossary: Schema fields
6619.content: Candidate terms extracted from every schema field with a doc comment: <Declaration>.<field> as the label, the comment’s first paragraph as the definition. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap-tools 44 (SKOS) · cat-harness-tools 2233 (SKOS) · fhir-harness 141 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 181 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-sci 49 (SKOS) · smart-base 13 (SKOS). Split by first letter. 2661 terms are too many for one page within its budget of 1.0 MB, so they are on 7 pages by the first letter of the label. The ranges are fixed, so a term’s address does not move as terms are added. A label that does not start with a letter is on the first page. | A–C: 492 terms | D–E: 211 terms | F–L: 525 terms | M–O: 213 terms | P–R: 517 terms | S: 248 terms | T–Z: 455 terms | .

6621.title: Glossary
6621.content: Every term the instances in this repository define or carry, as W3C SKOS. Terms link to the external concepts they match rather than copying them. 4352 terms: 41 authored in 6 glossaries, one page per instance that owns them, and 4229 extracted from knowledge-graph assets in 31 generated schemes, one page per asset type, plus the sources below. | state | what it means | terms | . | authored | A person wrote or approved the definition. | 41 | . | candidate, extracted | Lifted from a knowledge-graph asset's own title and description, verbatim, and not curated. The definition is the asset's text, the source links to the asset, and an asset with no description gives a term with none. A person promotes one by authoring it. | 4229 | . | could-not-extract | The source names a term the extractor could not read, and says why. | 0 | .

6622.title: Already somebody else’s concept?
6622.content: Extracted candidates are minted from this repository’s own assets and are not, by themselves, checked against any vocabulary. check:term-mapping asks whether each already exists as a concept somebody is authoritative for — SKOS for what a term MEANS, FHIR for a clinical code’s operational semantics — and the two are separate questions with separate answers. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 4311 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 4311 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin.

6623.title: Pages
6623.content: Each term is on exactly one page. Authored terms are on the page of the instance that owns their scheme (owner, 2026-10-15), and extracted candidates are split by asset type (owner, 2026-09-24), so that no page is fetched at the size of all of them. | page | holds | terms | size | . | this page | counts and sources | — | 14 KB | . | bootstrap | authored terms of bootstrap | 22 | 26 KB | . | cat-harness | authored terms of cat-harness | 14 | 17 KB | . | fhir-harness | authored terms of fhir-harness | 0 | 2 KB | . | folio-assistant-core | authored terms of folio-assistant-core | 4 | 10 KB | . | folio-assistant-sci | authored terms of folio-assistant-sci | 0 | 2 KB | . | smart-base | authored terms of smart-base | 0 | 2 KB | . | who-iris | authored terms of who-iris | 83 | 214 KB | . | Skills | candidates, extracted | 424 | 329 KB | . | Tools | candidates, extracted | 90 | 86 KB | . | BPMN activities | candidates, extracted | 1039 | 831 KB | . | DMN decisions | candidates, extracted | 15 | 12 KB | . | Schema fields | candidates, extracted | 2661 | 1.5 MB | . Size: this page is 14 KB before compression, within its budget of 64 KB; each instance’s and each asset type’s page has a budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter on each page runs over that page, and its A–Z bar jumps within it. The SKOS files in the sources are the machine-readable form.

7361.title: bibliography/ page: as-is intent
7361.content: Covers: the bibliography visualiser folio-assistant-core declares in folio-assistant-core.json (renderedBy: bibliography-page, coversKinds: [references, catalogue], subgraphs: directory), routed at en/folio-assistant-core/bibliography/ (the old unlocalised address forwards there). It is generated by folio-assistant-core/scripts/bibliography-page.ts (bun run cat bibliography:page, the bibliography-page Tool) and gated by check:bibliography (bean folio-assistant-63q4, folio-assistant-core#88). Candidate: as-is.html, the index page, with the page of one sub-graph drawn below it. Checked at web 1280 and mobile 390. Who it is for: a reader or an author of a folio who wants a reference the knowledge graph holds, whether a folio cites it (a references node) or a catalogue holds it (a Dublin Core record). Owner, 2026-10-14: “there should be a bibliography viewer that allows view/export in multiple formats of bib items in the folio … also be able to export biblio reference for a single asset/paper … biblio viewer should work similar to glossary viewer … use path limit to subgraphs and specific assets”. What they need to do: find a reference, read its citation, see where it came from and whether the library holds it, and export the whole list, one sub-graph’s list, or one reference, in the format their tool reads. What it must show, as the generator writes it: . On the index (<route>/): . | what the page holds: references directories’ folio-reference/v1 nodes and catalogue directories’ Dublin Core records, as one list; | the export of every reference shown: BibTeX, CSL-JSON, RIS and Dublin Core / BIBO JSON-LD, as files beside the page; | a “By sub-graph” line linking each declared directory’s page, with its count; | a filter box with a live count; | per reference, in an ordered list: the citation (up to three authors then “et al.”, year, title, container, volume, issue, pages, publisher); its key as a link to its own anchor; its provenance (catalogue or authored); its DOI or URL; its ISBN; the source file it was read from; where the library holds it; and its own export as BibTeX, RIS and CSL-JSON downloads. | . On each sub-graph’s page (<route>/<sub-graph>/): the directory, its instance and kind, a link back to all references, the same four exports over that directory alone, and the filter and list.

7362.title: Observed on the branch
7362.content: In the folio-assistant index at the claude/b1-step4-trial pins with core’s main: 3 references, all from one sub-graph, the IRIS replica’s catalogue (three Dublin Core records of its catalogue/, each held in its library/). The index page is 12.5 KB. A checkout that mounts a folio with a bibliography (qou’s alone is 915 references) has many more, on the same layout. At 390 px the source paths and the keys wrap anywhere rather than widening the page.

What they need to do: find a term fast, read its definition, see its code, see which external concept it matches, and tell an authored definition from a candidate extracted from a knowledge-graph asset. What it must show: . On the index (glossary/): . | the counts by state (authored, candidate extracted, could-not-extract); | a Pages table: this page and one row per asset type (skills, Tools, BPMN activities, DMN decisions, schema fields), each linked, with its term count and size; | the index’s own size and its budget (64 KB), and the per-type budget (1 MB); | the authored terms, with a filter box and live count, and an A–Z letter bar; | per term: the label, the code (notation) when the label and source do not already say it, a status badge when not authored, the definition, the scheme, the term IRI for an authored term, the source as a link to the asset, and the external matches as links; | a Sources list: each scheme with its SKOS JSON-LD link, the swimlane ledgers (linked, never copied), and the external schemes referenced through remoteGraphs; | a table of the extracted schemes, instance by asset type, each column heading linked to that type’s page and each count linked to its SKOS; | schema.org DefinedTermSet JSON-LD for search engines, carrying the authored terms only. | . On each asset type’s page (glossary/<type>/): . | a link back to the index, and a sentence on what the terms are read from; | which instances contribute, each with its count and SKOS link; | the page’s size and its budget; | the filter box with a live count, the A–Z bar, and every term with the “candidate, extracted” badge. | . Every term is on exactly one page: authored on the index, extracted on its type’s.

9031.title: Chaque flux de travail du dépôt
9031.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR . Combien y a-t-il de fichiers BPMN 2.0 ? Cette page ne l’indique plus, et c’est là une correction plutôt qu’une dérobade. La phrase qui ouvrait cette section comportait un décompte, et elle a été fausse cinq fois de suite — « six », puis « dix-neuf », puis « trente », puis « trente-deux, tous sous processes/ », puis « trente-neuf » — chacune assez longtemps pour être erronée, et découverte à chaque fois par quelqu’un qui a exécuté ls par hasard. La dernière de ces affirmations comportait une erreur de seize lorsqu’elle a enfin été vérifiée : elle en annonçait trente-neuf alors qu’il y en avait cinquante-cinq. Un décompte en prose est une affirmation ; un index dérivé est une preuve. Le nombre réside donc dans l’index dérivé des processus, qui est généré à partir de la déclaration par bun run cat auto:docs, contrôlé en CI, et ne peut pas diverger des diagrammes qu’il dénombre. Le rôle de cette page est la moitié qui ne peut pas être générée — à quoi sert chaque processus, dans quel cas vous vous y trouveriez, et quel processus voisin vous recherchez réellement. Cette séparation est la règle de la compétence auto-docs, et cette page en est l’exemple concret : l’index indique ce qui existe et ce que chaque diagramme déclare à propos de lui-même ; tout ce qui suit détaille ce que l’index ne peut structurellement pas exprimer. Les diagrammes d’amorçage (bootstrap) sont délibérément exclus de cet index, et leur absence est un choix délibéré plutôt qu’une omission. bootstrap/workflows/ est déclaré par bootstrap/bootstrap.json et non par la racine, car le déclarer à cet endroit réintroduirait le processus d’amorçage dans le graphe publié de la racine — ce que #432 a délibérément supprimé et qu’un test protège toujours. Le bean pve3 conserve ce choix : les deux moitiés de bootstrap, ou aucune des deux. Ainsi, l’index dérivé couvre ce que la racine déclare, et les trois diagrammes d’amorçage sont nommés à la place dans le tableau ci-dessous. Chacun est un véritable document BPMN 2.0 avec interchange de diagrammes (BPMN DI) — ouvrez-le dans bpmn.io, Camunda Modeler ou tout autre outil BPMN. Les SVG présents dans la documentation sont générés à partir de ces fichiers par bun run cat render:bpmn ; ne modifiez jamais un SVG à la main. Avant tout le reste — le processus qu’une personne rencontre en premier, et le seul qui s’exécute lorsqu’aucun folio n’existe encore. Ce tableau mentionnait bootstrap/workflows/bootstrap.bpmn jusqu’au 2026-09-20 — un fichier qui n’existe pas, renommé en initialize-harness.bpmn bien avant — tandis que les trois véritables diagrammes n’étaient pas nommés. Une référence orpheline cachée derrière un répertoire que rien n’analysait, ce qui est précisément ce que la vérification des éléments non indexés a pour vocation de détecter et n’a pas pu faire, car elle ne pouvait pas non plus voir ce répertoire (bean 7u3g). Les lignes sont désormais correctes. Les diagrammes demeurent invisibles pour les outils, et ce délibérément en attente d’une décision : bootstrap/workflows/ est déclaré par bootstrap/bootstrap.json mais pas par la racine, et le déclarer là-bas réintroduirait le processus d’amorçage dans le graphe publié de la racine — ce que #432 a délibérément supprimé et qu’un test protège toujours. Le bean pve3 consigne ce choix : les deux moitiés de bootstrap, ou aucune des deux. | Diagramme | Questions traitées | . | bootstrap/workflows/bootstrap.bpmn | Un agent a été orienté vers un dépôt et ne sait rien. Est-ce déjà une instance — la charger — ou non, auquel cas que doit-elle devenir ? La seule entrée est une référence d’instance ; le type de harness, le graphe de connaissances et la voix sont lus depuis la déclaration de cette instance. Voir bootstrap/README.md et la proposition | . | bootstrap/workflows/initialize-harness.bpmn | Un agent a été orienté vers un dépôt et ne sait rien. Le seul processus d’amorçage qu’un acteur DÉMARRE — un agent d’amorçage (Bootstrapping Agent) ayant lu bootstrap/README.md se trouve à son événement de début et n’a nulle part ailleurs où commencer. Trois couloirs : Bootstrapping Agent, Requestor, et Knowledge Graph Data Store. Voir bootstrap/README.md et la proposition | . | bootstrap/workflows/discussion.bpmn | Deux faits n’ont aucune réponse dans un fichier accessible à un agent d’amorçage — quel harness ce dépôt doit devenir, et quels dépôts sont lus et écrits. Ce sont des jugements portés par la personne qui a demandé le harness, donc aucun corps d’instruction ne les produit. On y entre depuis initialize-harness lorsqu’un tel fait est requis, ce qui explique pourquoi bootstrap contient un second processus : il est présupposé par chaque tâche plutôt qu’indiqué par une seule | . | bootstrap/workflows/log-message.bpmn | Un sous-processus, jamais un point d’entrée — atteint par une activité d’appel, jamais démarré, raison pour laquelle le README de bootstrap peut continuer d’affirmer qu’il n’y a qu’un seul processus que vous commencez. Appelable facultativement depuis n’importe quelle tâche (un acteur consignant ce qu’il fait n’a besoin d’aucune autorisation) ou requis par un diagramme qui dessine l’appel explicitement ; même sous-processus dans les deux cas, la seule différence étant si l’appelant l’a représenté ou non. Il réside dans bootstrap plutôt que dans le harness car bootstrap ne peut pas importer le harness, de sorte qu’un enregistreur défini en amont serait inutilisable par l’acteur ayant le plus besoin d’indiquer ce qu’il fait | . | getting-started.bpmn | Quelqu’un a dit « créer un folio ». Laquelle des cinq choses voulait-il dire, et que faut-il vérifier avant d’écrire quoi que ce soit ? | . Sa passerelle d’intention est calculée, non choisie : decisions/folio-intent.dmn renvoie la branche, et ask fait partie des résultats possibles — ce qui rend la question obligatoire plutôt que de simple courtoisie. Voir Premiers pas. Indépendant du contenu — ces trois processus s’appliquent à chaque folio, et les processus extérieurs référencent les intérieurs sous forme d’activités d’appel, de sorte que chaque processus n’est décrit qu’une fois et réutilisé : . | Niveau | Diagramme | Questions traitées | . | 1 | Cycle de vie du contenu — content-lifecycle.bpmn | Un cycle d’un folio, planification → retrait | . | 2 | Brouillon → publication — draft-to-publication.bpmn | Comment le corpus devient un folio officiellement publié | . | 3 | Édition et validation IHM — editing-hci-validation.bpmn | Ce qui arrive à une modification proposée pour un bloc de contenu | . Spécifique au type de contenu — comment un type particulier de folio est rédigé. Ceux-ci se situent au sein de Rédiger la modification du bloc du niveau 3, et résident avec leurs guides : . | Diagramme | Type de contenu | Emplacement | . | authoring-a-document.bpmn | Documents et directives politiques | Rédiger un document | . | authoring-a-paper.bpmn | Articles scientifiques et livres | Rédiger un article | . | l2-dak-authoring.bpmn | DAK des directives SMART de l’OMS (L2) | Rédiger un DAK SMART de l’OMS | . | l3-fhir-pipeline.bpmn | Guide d’implémentation SMART de l’OMS (L3) | Rédiger un IG SMART de l’OMS | . | ig-incremental-build.bpmn | IG SMART de l’OMS (L3) — couloir de compilation, incrémentiel par cône de dépendances (proposé) | Rendre la compilation incrémentielle · vue d’ensemble | . Processus d’agent — fonctionnement d’un agent, plutôt que rédaction du contenu. Ceux-ci s’exécutent en parallèle des processus de contenu plutôt qu’à l’intérieur : . | Diagramme | Questions traitées | . | crdm-requirements.bpmn | Une demande de fonctionnalité est arrivée. Comment est-elle transformée en exigences validées, et qui signe l’approbation ? Le processus externe ; ses six phases sont les activités d’appel ci-dessous. Voir Méthodologie CRDM | . | crdm-issue-linking.bpmn | Rechercher un ticket correspondant, puis lier ou demander — un ticket n’est jamais créé sans l’autorisation du BA | . | crdm-needs.bpmn | Phase 1 : identifier les parties prenantes, synthétiser l’énoncé des besoins, boucler jusqu’à ce qu’il soit reconnu | . | crdm-requirements-definition.bpmn | Phases 2–4 : cartographier le flux actuel, définir les exigences et leur impact, boucler jusqu’à approbation | . | crdm-data-model.bpmn | Entre les exigences et l’approbation : entités issues du BPA et des exigences, cardinalités indiquées dans les deux sens, en bouclant jusqu’à ce que le BA reconnaisse les entités ET que les parties prenantes aient répondu à chaque cardinalité | . | crdm-signoff.bpmn | Phase 5 : les exigences deviennent des beans, le BA signe l’approbation, la branche est annoncée sur le ticket | . | crdm-deliver.bpmn | Phase 6 : implémenter, examiner l’incrément, partager le MVP, recueillir les retours des parties prenantes. Une seule phase, car les trois boucles reviennent vers l’implémentation | . | crdm-close.bpmn | Validation des parties prenantes, confirmation du BA, et clôture seulement ensuite — un agent ne présume jamais de l’achèvement | . | diig-investment-path.bpmn | Le Guide d’investissement dans la mise en œuvre des interventions numériques (DIIG) de l’OMS sous forme de processus : neuf chapitres allant de la constitution de l’équipe à la proposition de valeur, avec les PROPRES points d’étape du Guide à 4.5 et 8.5 sous forme de passerelles plutôt que de points de contrôle ajoutés ici. Le chapitre 3 s’appuie sur le CRDM, raison pour laquelle il figure à côté des diagrammes ci-dessus. Réside dans smart-base, car une méthode métier appartient au dépôt propriétaire du domaine | . | bean-lifecycle.bpmn | Quand un agent crée-t-il, modifie-t-il ou abandonne-t-il un bean — et pourquoi un bean n’est-il jamais supprimé ? Voir Beans et tâches | . | session-state-machine.bpmn | Un agent déroulant une machine à états, maintenant le contexte d’une session à jour tout au long d’une discussion. La structure est stricte — l’interpréteur prend en charge neuf types d’éléments et lève une exception sur les autres — et ce qui varie est la branche active choisie par l’agent. Les deux passerelles portent l’annotation cat-harness.processes:judgement, marqueur introduit avec ce diagramme pour que « pas de tableau car il s’agit d’une décision humaine » cesse d’être indiscernable de « pas encore de tableau ». La machine enregistre qu’un bean a été pris en charge ; elle n’en prend jamais un d’elle-même | . | activity-log.bpmn | Quand un agent écrit-il une entrée de journal, et quand est-elle conservée ? La persistance est désactivée par défaut, et la passerelle lit un paramètre à trois états — off, on, unknown — au lieu de deviner. Vider le journal est la seule exception à la règle de non-suppression qui régit le reste de fsh-guts/ | . | content-change-review.bpmn | La modification d’un auteur, de sa description à son approbation par le comité de relecture en passant par la mise en préproduction (staging) | . | code-change-review.bpmn | La même boucle pour une modification de la plateforme plutôt que du contenu : prise en charge, branche, passage des portes de validation, ouverture de la PR dès le premier commit, passage de la CI au vert, traitement des retours de relecture, fusion. Dessiné pour le bean haya après qu’un audit a constaté qu’INTEGRATION et VERIFICATION n’avaient pas de propriétaire — non par manque de vocabulaire, mais parce que le diagramme ci-dessus prend pour objet une modification de contenu. Aucun couloir de déploiement : c’est la seule partie dont les activités diffèrent selon chaque topologie | . | qa-report-signing.bpmn | Attestation d’un rapport QA, selon l’une des deux voies choisies à partir des faits déclarés : un signataire API lorsque l’acteur exécutant dispose de la connectivité réseau requise, une autorité humaine de publication sinon. Bean r0rq, pour le cas soulevé par le responsable — « une API ne marcherait pas et un acteur humain est nécessaire ». La branche est calculée par decisions/signing-route.dmn, qui lit la portée d’accès (reach) de l’acteur et la configuration d’un point de terminaison ; une portée non déclarée vaut unknown et achemine vers la personne, car une passerelle qui supposerait « connecté » produirait un rapport non signé ayant l’apparence d’un rapport signé | . | actor-role-administration.bpmn | Modifier qui peut faire quoi : ajouter un acteur et déclarer son type, ouvrir ou fermer un rôle, accorder ou révoquer une permission, retirer un acteur sans le supprimer — puis auditer. Bean hb2o : la jointure est propre (31 rôles sur 31 lient un couloir, aucune référence orpheline), il s’agissait donc d’un processus manquant, et non d’un processus défectueux. Il appelle code-change-review pour la branche, les portes et la relecture plutôt que de les redéfinir, et ajoute les trois éléments spécifiques à l’édition du socle auquel chaque autre diagramme se rattache. Le rôle administrator a attendu que le responsable indique que l’administration constitue un couloir — un rôle n’est jamais inventé pour rendre un diagramme traçable | . | graph-detanglement.bpmn | Une partie d’un dépôt doit être détachée — pour des raisons de taille ou sémantiques. Les quatre étapes sont des portes infranchissables plutôt que de simples recommandations, et c’est la raison même d’être de ce diagramme : graph-detanglement.md indique en prose que « rien ne bouge tant que l’étape précédente n’est pas mesurée à zéro », et la prose est précisément ce qu’un agent sous pression contourne par le discours. Les trois passerelles s’appuient sur DMN, de sorte que l’achèvement refuse tout résultat fourni manuellement et que la branche est calculée à partir de décomptes déjà générés par un outil. La plus stricte est Detangled?, et elle l’est en raison de son ORDRE DE RÈGLES — unassignedEdges > 0 renvoie unknown avant même que la règle des arêtes croisées ne soit évaluée, si bien qu’un décompte d’arêtes croisées nul sur un corpus non évalué ne peut être interprété comme un succès. Chaque porte dispose d’un troisième état et aucune ne le considère comme réussi : les deux chemins unknown sont un REFUS d’avancer plutôt qu’un avertissement. Authorise the extraction se trouve dans le couloir Administrator car déplacer des artefacts durables hors d’un dépôt relève de la décision d’une personne — l’agent signale ce qui serait déplacé et attend, conformément à deletion-requires-confirmation | . Relecture — l’entrée générique et les deux spécialisations dans lesquelles elle descend. Ce sont des processus distincts plutôt que des compétences supplémentaires portées par le relecteur, car la pile de sous-processus a une PORTÉE DÉLIMITÉE : un acteur n’endosse le rôle du couloir intérieur que pour ce chemin d’appel précis, alors qu’inherits propagerait les deux spécialisations partout. | Diagramme | Questions traitées | . | review-task.bpmn | Quel type d’élément a été modifié, et vers quelle relecture descend-on ? | . | review-narrative.bpmn | Prose : registre et voix, dépendances éditoriales requises pour le lecteur, traduction | . | review-code.bpmn | Nœuds de code du graphe : définitions d’outils et nœuds de définition de schéma — le nœud déclare-t-il ce qu’il est, ses références sont-elles résolues, le mécanisme qu’il annonce est-il celui qui s’exécute ? | . | options-analysis.bpmn | Une décision comportant des alternatives : quelle méthodologie adoptée s’applique ici, quelles étaient les options, et pourquoi les options rejetées ont-elles été écartées ? Appelé sous forme de sous-processus, son déclencheur est celui d’opening-brief — l’irréversibilité et la surprise, non la taille — de sorte qu’un choix réversible s’arrête dès la première tâche et qu’un choix irréversible ne peut pas l’ignorer. Il ne tranche pas : il produit les options et une recommandation, l’autorisation appartenant à l’étape appelante. | . | swot-analysis.bpmn | Analyse de situation avant une décision : ce qui caractérise les attributs propres d’un sujet (forces, faiblesses) et son environnement (opportunités, menaces), croisés dans les stratégies candidates SO/WO/ST/WT. Aucun chemin ne prend de décision — c’est le refus explicite de la méthode swot, représenté afin de ne pas pouvoir être ignoré, et chaque exécution terminée enregistre une situation ou transmet les candidats non classés à options-analysis. L’externe est analysé avant l’interne, selon Weihrich tel que la source ingérée le rapporte. Il ne classe pas ce qu’il trouve, la méthode n’ayant aucun moyen de le faire. | . | voice-review.bpmn | Quelles voix éditoriales nommées ce folio a-t-il ACTIVÉES, et la citation propre à chaque règle étaye-t-elle le constat émis ? Appelé depuis review-narrative.bpmn, il se termine immédiatement lorsqu’aucune voix n’est active — ce qui est le comportement par défaut et le cas de cette instance. | . | adjudication.bpmn | La relecture n’a abouti à aucun accord mécanique ni consensus, un jugement est donc nécessaire — ainsi que les traces qu’il doit laisser. Déclenché uniquement lorsque les évaluations des relecteurs sur un critère SONT EN DÉSACCORD, ce que block-qa/v1 rend calculable, de sorte que la première passerelle quitte le processus plutôt que de deviner : un relecteur sans vérificateur constitue une relecture, un vérificateur sans relecteur constitue une porte de contrôle. Conçu pour le bean 7pdi après que cette structure a été trouvée implémentée sept fois — cinq activités d’arbitrage à travers processes/, plus /api/relevance/adjudicate et bib-verification.ts, qui ne partagent aucun code avec les diagrammes et ont abouti à la même règle. Consultatif, car un jugement ne peut faire l’objet d’une porte automatisée ; Write the entry that LEADS et Grant a dispensation, with its reason ne sont pas assouplissables, car un jugement non consigné par écrit est indiscernable d’un vérificateur qui n’a jamais été exécuté | . | narrative-code-review.bpmn | Une modification a touché les deux côtés d’une paire prose ↔ code déclarée — un diagramme et le flux de travail qu’il implémente, une compétence et le code adjacent — review-task l’envoie donc ici, la seule branche qui confronte les deux volets l’un à l’autre. La machine a déjà tourné (prose-reviewed-since-code-changed et prose-claims-resolve sur le sidecar) ; le relecteur ne tranche que ce que celles-ci ont laissé en suspens, selon l’une des trois voies : attester avec un motif, émettre un constat contre le mauvais côté, ou — en cas de désaccord avec un vérificateur — appeler criterion-adjudication. Conçu pour le ticket #1042, étape C ; le cas Lean relève de proof-narrative-lean-equivalence, non de ce diagramme | . | folio-assistant-core/processes/library/deep-document-research.bpmn | Répondre à une question à partir d’un corpus que ce folio détient DÉJÀ, de manière itérative, et s’arrêter sur une condition explicite. Restitue Doc-Researcher (arXiv:2510.21603v1, Dong et al.) sous forme de processus : filtrer le corpus et choisir la granularité, chercher, affiner, puis évaluer la suffisance. Deux voies de sortie, toutes deux capitales — un seuil seul ne se termine jamais sur une question à laquelle le corpus ne peut répondre, un plafond seul interrompt prématurément une question soluble et renvoie un résultat d’apparence complète — et la condition déclenchée est transmise au rapport. UN seul couloir, non les quatre agents de l’article : il s’agit de quatre questions relevant d’une même responsabilité, et le modèle de rôles de ce dépôt fait d’un couloir une responsabilité. Synthesise, cite to a location, and say what was not found n’est pas assouplissable, car une recherche terminée en silence ressemble trait pour trait à une recherche réussie | . | criterion-adjudication.bpmn | La spécialisation critère-QA de l’arbitrage : solliciter le jugement partagé, puis exécuter l’une des trois actions admises par un désaccord sur un critère — le constat est maintenu, le critère est restreint afin de cesser de s’appliquer ici, ou il s’applique et une dérogation en consigne la raison.
